content.text:
All 971 tests pass, and `flutter analyze` reports zero issues.

## Summary

**Investigation first:** I ruled out the obvious client-side timeout misconfiguration — the existing uncommitted `receiveTimeout: Duration.zero` fix in `api_client.dart` is correctly implemented (verified line-by-line against dio 5.11.1's actual source) and does disable the stream-read timeout, but it only guards against generations taking **>30 seconds**. That's a different bug from the one you're hitting, which is why the earlier correction session didn't change anything for you.

The evidence that actually fits — empty bubble, failure within ~2s on *every* message, nothing in console, and critically the duplicate-question-on-retry (which only happens when `message_created` never arrived, i.e. zero SSE events were ever read) — points to a stale pooled connection. `ChatCubit.init()` fires `chat-sessions-list`/`chat-messages-list` on every mount, which (via dio's default `dart:io` keep-alive pooling) leaves an open connection to the backend host. By the time you finish typing and hit send, that idle pooled connection has very plausibly been torn down on the server/edge side — common on a real Wi-Fi path against serverless edge infra, essentially never reproducible on localhost/simulator or in a fresh one-off curl/Postman call (which never reuses this app's pool).

**Fix applied** ([api_client.dart](lib/core/network/api_client.dart)): `postStream` now sets `persistentConnection: false`, forcing a brand-new connection for every chat send/retry instead of racing a possibly-dead pooled one. I also added `debugPrint` calls on the stream's error paths — previously every failure here was swallowed completely silently, which is exactly why nothing showed up in your console. If this doesn't fully resolve it, the next reproduction will now print the real `DioException` type/message.

**What I couldn't do:** there's no device/simulator wired into this environment (per `AGENTS.md`), so I can't personally send a message on your physical iPhone to confirm end-to-end. Tests (189 chat/network + full suite of 971) and `flutter analyze` are clean, but you'll need to rebuild onto your iPhone and send a real question to verify. If it still fails, the new `debugPrint` output in the Flutter/Xcode console will tell us the exact exception this time instead of nothing.

content.text:
All green — 110 chat tests pass, `flutter analyze` is clean. ## Root cause Confirmed directly from the frozen prototype (`cerne-prototype.html`), the AI message block's own markup: ```html
{{ msg.text }}
Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente {{ msg.time }}
``` The `{{ msg.time }}` span sits **outside** the failure-note's `sc-if` — it's unconditional. The failed state is supposed to show the red retry note *and* the gray mono time caption stacked below it, not one in place of the other. [chat_bubble.dart:200-203](lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart#L200-L203) had them as mutually exclusive (`if failed → retry indicator, else → time caption`) — a prior pass's doc comments explicitly (and incorrectly) claimed the retry note "replaces the timestamp slot." ## Fix Changed the two to render together: the retry indicator only when `failed`, then the time caption unconditionally after it. The retry indicator's existing `chatFailureIndicatorPadding` bottom inset (`spacingXs` = 4px) already supplies exactly the gap the prototype's `gap:4px` flex container specifies, so no extra spacing widget was needed. I also corrected the stale doc comments that described the old (wrong) behavior, and updated/extended the existing widget test (`chat_bubble_test.dart`) to assert the timestamp caption ("agora") is now present alongside the retry note in the failed state — it was passing before only because it never checked for the caption's absence. This is a pure Flutter-widget-tree visual fix with no device-specific network behavior involved, so the test suite is a reliable end-to-end confirmation here (unlike the previous network-layer fix). If you want to eyeball it on the simulator/device too, trigger a failed AI response and confirm the gray `HH:mm`/"agora" caption now appears directly under the red retry note.

Você recebeu o argumento `<ID>`, onde `<ID>` é um de: `SETUP`, `PLAN`, `F000`, `RF01`…`RF10`.

**Se `<ID>` não foi fornecido, ou não é exatamente um desses valores: PARE. Não adivinhe, não infira pelo que estava sendo discutido na sessão. Pergunte ao usuário qual ID usar e espere a resposta antes de rodar qualquer coisa.** Gravar o ID errado corrompe a atribuição de tempo/tokens por unidade de trabalho (M1-M3) — é um erro sério, não um detalhe.

Rode exatamente este comando, pelo caminho absoluto (nunca relativo — esta skill roda de dentro do repositório do ciclo, não de `cerne-avaliacao`), substituindo `<ID>` pelo argumento recebido e `<CICLO>` por `a` ou `b` conforme o `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` desta sessão (`cfg-ciclo-a` → `a`; `cfg-ciclo-b` → `b`):

python3 /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-avaliacao/scripts/coletar_sessao.py skill <ID> --ciclo <CICLO> --versao-claude-code "$(claude --version)" --config-raciocinio "$CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL" --otel-output ~/cerne/otelcol/output.jsonl
